environment.description: Same Rails application deployed on GKE with Istio service mesh. Envoy sidecar proxy has a custom Lua filter (istio-grpc-meta-sanitizer) that strips any metadata key matching patterns outside an explicit allowlist (x-request-id, x-b3-*, x-envoy-*, traceparent). The dashboard template's script tags include integrity attributes computed at deploy-time via a Sprockets preprocessor that generates SHA-384 hashes for all whitelisted CDN URLs stored in config/sri_manifest.yml. The Rails asset pipeline helper content_security_hash() performs a lookup against this manifest and returns 'sha384-<hash>' for known URLs; for ANY URL not in the manifest, it returns a deliberately invalid hash ('sha384-AAAA...') causing the browser to refuse loading. Additionally, the pod's NetworkPolicy restricts egress from the Rails container to only the three known gRPC service IPs on ports 50051-50053, preventing any metadata-manipulated routing to attacker-controlled backends.

config.envoy_lua_filter: strips non-allowlisted gRPC metadata keys before forwarding to upstream
config.sri_manifest: config/sri_manifest.yml with deploy-time SHA-384 hashes for all valid script URLs
config.sri_fallback_behavior: returns invalid hash sha384-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA for unknown URLs
